title: String Operations (string library)
summary: The string library: searching (find/gmatch/gsub), cutting (sub), transforming (upper/lower/rep), formatting (format), and splitting (split) text.

methods.name: string.len
methods.description: Length of the string in bytes. Same as `#s`.

methods.name: string.sub
methods.description: Slice from index i to j (both inclusive, 1-based; negatives count from the end).

methods.name: string.find
methods.signature: string.find(s, pattern, init?, plain?) --> number?, number?, ...
methods.description: Find a pattern. Returns start and end indices, or nil. Pass `true` as 4th arg to treat pattern as plain text.

methods.name: string.gmatch
methods.description: Iterate all matches of a pattern — the workhorse for tokenizing.

methods.name: string.gsub
methods.signature: string.gsub(s, pattern, repl, n?) --> string, number
methods.description: Replace all (or n) matches. repl can be a string, table, or function.

methods.name: string.format
methods.description: C-style formatting: %d int, %s string, %f float, %.2f two decimals, %q quoted.

methods.name: string.split
methods.description: Luau addition. Split into an array on a separator (default whitespace). Empty string sep splits every character.

methods.name: string.rep
methods.description: Repeat s n times, optionally with separator.

methods.name: string.byte / char
methods.description: Convert between characters and numeric codes.

details.heading: Pattern characters
details.body: Patterns are Lua's lightweight regex: `%a` letters, `%d` digits, `%w` alphanumerics, `%s` whitespace, `.` any char, `+` one or more, `*` zero or more, `?` optional, `^`/`$` anchors, `%` escapes magic characters (e.g. `%(`, `%.`, `%%`).

details.heading: Method-call sugar
details.body: You can call these with colon syntax on any string: `s:upper()`, `s:find("x")`, `s:split(",")`.

explanation.whatItIs: A toolbox of functions that inspect and transform text. Anything from 'does this chat message contain a banned word?' to 'parse this comma-separated list' is built from these.
explanation.whyItExists: Raw string values are rarely exactly what you need — you need parts of them, cleaned versions, or formatted versions.
whenToUse: `find` to test whether text contains something: `msg:find("help")`
`split` to break input into pieces: command parsing
`format` for assembling numbers and text into UI strings
whenNotToUse: Don't reach for patterns when `plain` matching or `split` suffices — patterns are powerful but cryptic
Don't use gsub where a simple `if s:find(...)` answers the question
tips: Always pass `true` to `find` when searching user text, so characters like `.` or `%` aren't treated as pattern magic
`for word in text:gmatch("%S+") do` iterates words
`string.format("%02d:%02d", m, s)` is the classic timer formatter
commonMistakes: Forgetting `find` returns two values (start AND end), so `if s:find(x) then` is correct but treating the result as a boolean-ish index confuses people
Pattern magic chars biting you: `"100%":find("%")` errors unless escaped `%%` or plain=true
Indices in `sub`/`find` are 1-based and inclusive on both ends

examples.title: Parsing a simple command
examples.code:
local input = "give sword 3"
local parts = input:split(" ")

local command = parts[1]      --> "give"
local item = parts[2]         --> "sword"
local amount = tonumber(parts[3]) or 1

print(command, item, amount)  --> give  sword  3
examples.whyItWorks: `split(" ")` turns the raw message into an array you can index. `tonumber` safely converts the amount with a fallback.

examples.title: Censoring words with gsub
examples.code:
local banned = {"noob", "lag"}

local function censor(text)
    for _, word in banned do
        text = text:gsub(word, string.rep("#", #word))
    end
    return text
end

print(censor("wow such noob lag"))   --> wow such #### ###

examples.title: Safe plain search
examples.code:
local message = "Meet me at 50% power!"
-- plain=true so '%' is not treated as a pattern escape
if message:find("50%", 1, true) then
    print("Found it")
end
